data.title: Chadchart defends switch to electric rubbish trucks
data.description: City Hall has defended a plan to replace rented diesel rubbish trucks with electric vehicles, saying the switch could cut energy costs by about 4.75 billion baht, or 54%, over five years.

data.title: B95bn irrigation project gets nod
data.description: A six-year irrigation project worth 95 billion baht has been approved to improve flood management in the lower eastern Chao Phraya basin and protect communities and economic areas across eight provinces, including Bangkok, said the government.

data.title: New rules clarify emergency care rights
data.description: The cabinet has endorsed revised rules for the Universal Coverage for Emergency Patients (UCEP) scheme, reaffirming that critically ill emergency patients must receive treatment without being charged until they are out of danger, for up to 72 hours.

data.title: CIB uncovers ex-abbot's millions
data.description: The Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) has uncovered more than 300 million baht in bank accounts linked to former Wat Phutthaisawan abbot Atichot Tanprasert and his close female associate as it widens its probe into suspected financial misconduct.

data.title: Anutin files defamation lawsuit against iLaw chief
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has filed a defamation lawsuit against iLaw director Yingcheep Atchanont over remarks linking him to alleged collusion in the 2024 Senate election, insisting the legal action is not intended to silence his critics.

data.title: Accused senators vow to fight charges
data.description: Senators accused of irregularities in the 2024 Senate election have vowed to fight the charges after the Election Commission (EC) decided to refer cases against 77 people, including 26 serving senators, to the Supreme Court.

data.title: Udon Thani counting down to international horticultural expo
data.description: Udon Thani is preparing to welcome visitors from Thailand and around the world to an international horticultural exposition starting on Nov 1 and running until March 14 next year.

data.title: Si Rat-Outer Ring Road tolls to rise from Dec 15
data.description: Tolls on the Prachim Ratthaya Expressway, also known as the Si Rat-Outer Ring Road Expressway, will increase by 15-35 baht from Dec 15, with the rate for four-wheel vehicles rising from 65 baht to 80 baht in accordance with the terms of the concession agreement.

data.title: Smuggled coffee seizures a first in southern Thailand
data.description: Customs officials in southern Thailand have seized more than 20 tonnes of illegally imported green coffee beans this year, as part of a wider crackdown that has resulted in seizures of goods worth 216 million baht.

data.title: Bedridden old woman carried 9km through rain to the bank
data.description: KANCHANABURI - Neighbours carried a bedridden 90-year-old woman on a stretcher for about 9 kilometres through heavy rain so she could rectify a problem with her ATM card at a bank branch in Sangkhla Buri district.

data.title: Use of banned ‘red meat’ chemicals in cattle uncovered
data.description: Thai authorities have arrested a chemical supplier after finding salbutamol, a beta agonist used illegally as a “red meat” enhancer, in nearly 1,000 cattle in an eight-month investigation spanning five provinces.

data.title: Cambodia ‘playing the victim’ in sea dispute, says Thailand
data.description: Thailand accused Cambodia on Tuesday of playing the victim in their dispute over maritime resources, as the Southeast Asian neighbours took their feud to international mediators a year after deadly clashes over their land border.

data.title: AC condensation, undersized screws caused parliament ceiling collapse
data.description: Water dripping from air conditioning ducts and undersized screws used in ceiling panels caused the ceiling of the cafeteria at the parliament complex in Bangkok to collapse on Sunday, an inspection has found.

data.title: Remains exhumed, moved from unlicensed Jewish cemetery
data.description: CHACHOENGSAO - Four bodies were exhumed at an unlicensed Jewish cemetery in Bang Khla district and moved to a licensed cemetery in adjoining Chon Buri province on Tuesday morning.

data.title: 'Hands off Koh Kut': Thailand stands firm at UN maritme talks
data.description: Thailand has made its position clear during maritime border talks with Cambodia under the UN law of the sea - Koh Kut is not part of the reconciliation process.

data.title: Chinese procurer fleeing prison in China arrested in Thailand
data.description: A 32-year-old Chinese woman allegedly fleeing a prison term in China for procuring women for prostitution has been arrested on a roadside near Suvarnabhumi airport after earlier entering Thailand illegally.

data.title: Chinese procuror fleeing prison in China arrested in Thailand
data.description: A 32-year-old Chinese woman allegedly fleeing a prison term in China for procuring women for prostitution has been arrested on a roadside near Suvarnabhumi airport after earlier entering Thailand illegally.

data.title: Illegal laughing gas factory busted in Bangkok
data.description: Bangkok police have shut down a Chinese-run factory in Prawet district that illegally produced and sold nitrous oxide, a mild anaesthetic also known as laughing gas and often used as a party drug.

data.title: Landslide damages school buildings in Nan, students relocated
data.description: NAN - An expanding landslide has forced the partial closure of a mountainside school, causing large cracks in a kindergarten building, a canteen, a shop and a swimming pool.

data.title: Phuket celebrates second Ganesh Chaturthi festival
data.description: PHUKET — Phuket started hosting its second Ganesh Chaturthi festival on Monday, bringing Thai and Indian communities together through religious ceremonies, cultural performances and a colourful procession through the historic Old Town.
